sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by flow cytometry in the context of a PGAP6-mediated GPI-AP shedding assay; tagged CRIPTO was shed from the cell surface by PGAP6, demonstrating it is correctly GPI-anchored and surface-localised. CRIPTO's own signalling function was not independently assayed in this study.
sites.rationale: CRIPTO is a GPI-anchored protein (topology: signal 1–30, extracellular 31–188, no TM helix), so the mature N-terminus after signal cleavage is the only extracellular terminus available for a surface tag. L1 explicitly describes a full-length human CRIPTO construct with an HA tag placed after the signal sequence at the N-terminus, stably expressed and detected on the HEK293T cell surface. Python confirms residue 30 is G and residue 31 is L, consistent with the signal-peptide boundary at position 30. No residue number is stated in the paper, so position_evidence is topology_derived rather than validated. Full-length human CRIPTO with an HA tag inserted after the signal sequence (residues 1–30) at the mature N-terminus was stably expressed in HEK293T cells (pME-pgkpuro-HA-CR1 construct). The same N-terminal HA-after-signal-sequence strategy was applied to a panel of human GPI-APs including CRIPTO using a CD59 signal sequence plus HA tag vector (L3). CRIPTO is a GPI-anchored protein with no TM domain; the mature N-terminus (residue 31) is the sole extracellular terminus, making insert_after_residue=30 the unique valid junction.

sources.claim: HEK293TcellsstablyexpressingHA-taggedCRIPTOwere established by transfection of linearized pME-pgkpuro-HACR1 and cultured in Dulbecco ’ s modified Eagle ’ s medium containing 10% fetal calf serum and 10 m g/ml puromycin as describedbefore(9).TopreparepME-pgkpuro-HA-CR1,we obtained human CRIPTO cDNA (Kazusa DNA Research Institute, Kisarazu, Japan) and cloned it into a mammalian expression plasmid pME bearing puromycin resistance gene and a segment of signal sequence plus HA tag.

literature_notes: L2 describes HA-tagged human CRYPTIC (CFC1, a paralog), not CRIPTO itself, tagged by the same N-terminal after-signal strategy; it corroborates the approach but L1 already directly covers CRIPTO, so L2 does not add a second independent site. L3 describes the same CRIPTO construct as L1 (N-terminal HA after CD59 signal sequence) and was used as corroborating evidence but is not a separate site. No ledger line names an internal loop insertion or a C-terminal tag for CRIPTO; the GPI anchor occupies the C-terminus (residues ~163–188 are the GPI-attachment signal), so a C-terminal surface tag is not supported by the ledger and would in any case be cleaved with the GPI signal. Only one site is reported.
